subject: Cooking
title: Biofuels and Fermentation: Brewing Energy
description: A 60-second lesson on Biofuels and Fermentation: Brewing Energy.

hook.text: The same yeast that makes beer can produce ethanol fuel. Fermentation powers cars, not just stomachs.

buildup.text: Bioethanol is made by fermenting sugarcane or corn — Brazil fuels 27% of its cars this way.

discovery.text: Scientists are engineering bacteria to ferment non-food waste into fuel — turning trash into energy.

twist.text: Corn ethanol uses almost as much energy to produce as it yields — its green credentials are debated.

climax.text: Next-gen fermentation targets algae and cellulose — feedstocks that don't compete with food supplies.

punchline.text: Ancient microbes may power the future.

quiz.question: What percentage of Brazil's cars run on fermented bioethanol?

details.summary: Biofuel production uses the same yeast fermentation that makes beer and wine, converting plant sugars into ethanol for fuel. Corn ethanol accounts for 10 percent of American gasoline.
details.whyItMatters: Biofuels connect ancient fermentation technology to modern energy challenges. The same microbial process that makes bread rise could reduce fossil fuel dependence if scaling challenges are overcome.
takeaways: Yeast converts plant sugars to ethanol using the same process as brewing
Corn ethanol makes up about 10 percent of US gasoline supply
Second-generation biofuels use agricultural waste instead of food crops

faq.question: How is biofuel fermentation related to beer brewing?
faq.answer: Both use yeast to convert sugars into ethanol through anaerobic fermentation. The biochemistry is identical. In brewing, ethanol is the desired product and CO2 is the byproduct. In biofuel production, the ethanol is collected as fuel instead of being consumed as a beverage.

faq.question: What are the challenges with corn-based ethanol as fuel?
faq.answer: Growing corn for fuel competes with food production and requires enormous amounts of water, fertilizer, and land. The energy returned barely exceeds the energy invested in production.
